text.p: Following are the main stories in Tuesday's Malaysian newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Saying that the government may have to call for a halt in the construction of more independent power plants, Prime Minister Mahathir Mohamad on Monday stressed that their owners should not burden Tenaga Nasional Bhd by demanding high prices for their electricity.

- Chief Minister of Kelantan Nik Abdul Aziz Nik Mat said he believed the walkout by state administrative officers at the last State Assembly was orchestrated by people who opposed the state government.

- Police have foiled a two million ringgit extortion attempt on the president-cum-chief executive officer of a public listed company with the arrest of a Malaysian suspected of operating from the United States. The company is a property concern listed on the Kuala Lumpur Stock Exchange's main board.

- The Securities Commission on Monday charged Repco Holdings Bhd chief executive officer Choo Chin Thye for giving a statement that is false or misleading, and which is likely to encourage the sale or purchase of Repco shares by others. Choo pleaded not guilty.
- The 1997 Budget is aimed at reducing the balance of payments deficit and stimulating growth in the Multimedia Super Corridor, Prime Minister Mahathir Mohamad said.
- President of the Kuala Lumpur Stock Exchange Salleh Majid said regulators will not restrict brokers from lending money to investors for the purchase of stocks on the exchange's second board.
- The Rashid Hussain Bhd (RHB) group is to make a bid for Kwong Yik Bank Bhd -- a move, if succssful, will propel the RHB Group into the big league of financial players, banking sources said.
